title: Migrate a long-running job from a status table and poller to AWS Lambda durable functions
description: Same job twice: a DynamoDB status table with a scheduled poller, then an AWS Lambda durable function with checkpointed steps and built-in retries. Same job id and GET API.

introBox.headline: How it works
text: A job too long or too fragile for one Lambda invocation is usually run through a hand-rolled status table: write a PENDING row, have a poller claim it, run the steps, update the row after each one, detect stale RUNNING rows, count attempts. This pattern deploys that version (before/) and the same job as a Lambda durable function (after/) side by side.

In the durable version each step is a context.step() call. The runtime checkpoints results, replays past completed steps after a crash, and retries the flaky step with a bounded createRetryStrategy() instead of a hand-written attempt counter.

The public job id becomes the DurableExecutionName, so starting a job is idempotent and GET /jobs/{id} resolves job_id to an execution ARN and reads status with GetDurableExecution. Durable statuses are mapped back to the old API's words so clients do not change.
Cutover: point POST at /v2, keep GET polling as is. The /v2 GET still answers for old rows while the legacy poller drains them; delete the legacy functions once no rows lack an execution ARN.
The durable half has Jest tests on the SDK's LocalDurableTestRunner, so the step wiring and retry can be verified without deploying.

bullets.text: Building fault-tolerant applications with Lambda durable functions
